Product Details can be found here:

http://www.litter-robot.com/litter-robot-accessories.aspx?categoryid=24

Initial impressions:

It arrived Saturday (so free shipping with Saturday delivery!) So I haven't had it a full 48 hours yet.

There are lots of videos out there that explain the mechanics in detail, so unless asked I'll only explain basics.

Extremely simplified: you fill the bottom of the globe with around 10lbs of litter (there is a fill mark). Cat steps inside, pressure sensor detects cats 5lbs or heavier. Once the cat leaves it triggers a variable timer (3,7 or 15 minutes). Cats re-entering will reset the timer. After timer expires it starts the clean cycle.

Clean cycle involves the globe spinning around. Clean litter passes through a grate and stored in a reservoir. Waste doesn't pass through grate, ends up going through a hole and then deposited into a waste bin. Waste bin uses standard 8-13gal bags.

I am extremely impressed with the build quality. It's an appliance really. It's not inexpensive, but the build quality feels like this thing should last for many years, and if the litter-robot 2 is any indicator, longevity shouldn't be an issue. Again, I really want to emphasize the solid construction of this thing. It's not heavy, but there are no loose parts, or flimsy pieces of plastic involved.

Cleaning cycle takes about 3 minutes.

The way it cleans the litter is so simple and efficient, that I really don't see how the process could fail unless the litter you bought doesn't clump at all. It has very few moving parts that can fail. Basically just the motor that spins the globe itself and some electronics for sensors. I'd like to emphasize this part, the design seems very conducive to many years of use with very little issues.

It's extremely efficient at removing only waste, so your litter should last longer (than other automatic cleaning devices). If you do need to remove all remaining litter, there is an empty button that makes it spin the opposite direction so that all litter goes into the waste bin instead of filtering into the reservoir.

I grabbed Dr Elseys Precious Cat clumping litter, and it is working extremely well so far.

A few problems with the Litter-Robot 2 (LR2) appear to have been addressed. The controls are off to the side, so they are no longer at risk of getting damaged from moisture (use your imagination). As the namesake suggests, the opening is much larger and much more open now, so bigger cats should have no issues (Even the LR2 was able to accommodate some fairly good sized cats). One of my 2 cats actually looks pretty small sitting inside it.

This also has a night mode. Press a button before you go to sleep and it will enable a night mode indefinitely until you shut it off or until it resets from power outage. With sleep mode enabled it wont do any clean cycles for 8 hours after you press the button, and it will repeat this every 24 hours. So if you press it at 8pm, it will keep going into sleep mode at 8pm every day going forward until you disable it or the power goes out.

It has a night light for low light locations (basements with no windows) or cats with bad eye sight. Night light can be turned off.

So this should work very well for people who have to keep this in their bedrooms.

New to the Open Air is a sensor telling you the tray is full. It will also stop operating (it will still do 3 more clean cycles) until you empty the tray and reset the unit. This addresses the single biggest issue people had with the LR2.

It's really not that noisy, I can barely hear it from an adjacent room. My RadioShack sound level meter, placed on the step, had it at 67 db. For comparison, an oscillating bedroom fan was measuring 72db on high. It's a constant whirring noise. No sudden clunks, etc, so light sleepers SHOULD be ok if it is allowed to clean through the night. Otherwise, just turn the night mode on.

There is also a battery backup option available for purchase. Unit runs on a battery (bigger battery, like out of a UPS) if power goes out. Great option if you are going on vacation.

I don't anticipate having to take advantage of the 90 day return policy. But if you do, you will have to pay shipping (which i feel is fair. no reason they have to pay for shipping both ways). I really can only see this being used if you just absolutely can't get your cats to use it. If you get a bad unit, then it really shouldn't be indicative of the product itself, contact support to fix it. It's worth it.

18 month warranty. With the LR2 they sell all kinds of replacement parts (motors, control boards, etc). I expect you'll see the same for the Open Air eventually.

My initial impressions are extremely positive. The only possible concern I see, is longevity. Many reviewers (on amazon, YouTube, etc) for the previous model (litter-robot) 2l mention they have had theirs for 4+ years with no issues (of manufacturing anyways). And like I said, there are no complicated moving parts involved that can fail.

If scooping litter is a real issue for you (due to health or just the fact that scooping litter really really really sucks), I really see no equal to the LR Open Air. Possibly the Cat Genie, but that requires plumbing and special litter. For elderly the litter-robot open air seems like an absolute home run. Maybe once every month or two, someone comes by to help clean the globe.

For comparison, I once had the PetSafe Simply Clean litter box. It lasted 1 week. My cat Sam kicks litter EVERYWHERE, and the PetSafe has a very very low brim. It also has a very complicated system where the whole base spins and there is a conveyor belt system taking waste up and into a waste bin. It worked, but it would get jammed up way too easily.

I've been using a standard litter box since then (first clumping then switched to non-clumping), and because of my work/travel schedule and other factors, it was turning into a real issue. I live alone and keeping up on the litter box for 2 cats was challenging for me. Litter everywhere, cats not using the litter box. The money spent on the open-air is a no brainer.

If you are in a similar situation, Take a serious look at the Open Air, or even the Litter Robot 2. You can get refurbished LR2 models for discounted price. Even with the refurbished models you still get 90 day return and 18 month warranty. Seriously, 18 month warranty with refurbished units. If that doesn't speak volumes about the company.

So, 23 days later how's it going? It seems your review is similarly positive to everything else about the company but you're one of only two reviews I could find on the LR 3 / Open Air.

I'm getting fed up with doing litterbox every day like a responsible adult with 2 cats and I'm debating between the refurbished LR2 and the new LR Open Air. Could you elaborate on why you picked the Open Air? Any concerns you have or changes you'd make?

Thanks!

I still can't believe how well it works. To date I've had ZERO issues, and unless there is a electrical or mechanical failure, I don't really see any reason why it wouldn't just keep chugging along. So truly, I just don't see anything that I would change about it. I haven't had to take the globe out to clean it yet, so ... maybe that will inspire something, but...not sure what :)

There are a few things with the Open Air that made me go with that vs the LR2. The new sensor that detects when the waste gets too high was the big one. With the LR2 a big complaint I kept seeing was waste getting smeared on the outside of the globe. The open air will run a few times AFTER it detects that it's full, then it stops, so you do have a little bit of a fair warning. LR2 also had problems with the front control buttons getting wet, and with the open air that's just not an issue anymore. It also has more options as for the timing it will start self cleaning. I still leave mine at the default 7 minutes. You may have litter that takes longer to clump, in which case, the longer wait time would be great to have. Also, I just really like the looks of the Open Air. It's really cool in person :) Is it worth the $150 or so over the LR2 refurbished models? If you don't mind keeping an eye on the LR2 more often, then...that's a bit of a tough sell. I kinda looked at it like this, the LR2 has been around for many many years. I'm sure they have learned a few things and other design improvements were made based on the LR2 that maybe they haven't really mentioned. Kinda like software, even if some of the fixes are little bugs, they are still fixing little bugs.

With my 2 cats, I'm changing the bag once a week and topping off the litter. I'm using Doctor Elseys right now. Still on my first 40lb bag.

Long story short, zero regrets, love it, my cats love it, it's saved my house, and for me the extra money for the Open Air wasn't a big issue. Would do again :) I also wouldn't hesitate for a second to recommend one of these for the elderly. It would be a god send for someone who can't really bend over or pick up a litter box on a regular basis.

Thanks for the quick and thorough reply! I think my only hesitation now is how cleaning this one compares with the LR 2. It seems like it's a little harder to get at the LR 3 globe to clean than the LR 2 was given that one just sat on the stand.

That said, I'll probably be springing for the LR3. I just need to poke around my apartment and make sure I have a space big enough for it somewhere out of the way!

The bonnet that goes over the top of the sphere is REALLY easy to remove. It's just held in with two clips on each side. Seriously only takes a few seconds to remove. At that point, I don't imagine there is much difference. This has a bigger opening, so maybe easier to clean? shrug Either way, that bonnet is a non-issue.

Now that I think about it, I also imagine that the bigger opening is much easier to fill. With the LR2 some people fill through the waste hole on the side of the sphere. They put it in "empty" mode so that hole is at the very top position. Otherwise you are probably scooping with a smaller cup or bowl to fill it from the front opening. But, with how often you are really filling the litter, this is hardly a factor either way.
